Private-project diagnostic · District 27 · generated 2026-07-25

Canberra Crescent Residences: launch evidence versus District 27

A sale-state-aware comparison of the 376-unit launch against Canberra, Sembawang and Yishun condominiums, followed by a diagnostic for every official district transaction in the current URA extract.

← All research reports Poiz versus East comparison
340official Canberra Crescent caveats through 2026-07; 1 in the partial month
90.4%caveats divided by 376 units—not confirmed sales or unique buyers
S$1,996subject median achieved PSF through the latest complete month
2,884official District 27 apartment/condominium records analysed row by row
61mstraight-line subject diagnostic to Canberra (NS12); not a walking route
Decision read: Start with The Watergardens and The Commodore for micro-location and newer-lease context, then Canberra Residences for the age/space discount. Use North Park, The Wisteria and Nine Residences only to test the separate value of established mixed-use integration. Never present the subject’s launch-month price path as resale appreciation.

Recommended comparison strategy

01

Micro-location first

Anchor on The Watergardens and The Commodore. They test recent 99-year Canberra precinct pricing with the least location drift.

Open strategy workbook →

02

Control for newness

Use Canberra Residences as the older same-precinct control. Its lower PSF can come with larger layouts and a shorter remaining lease.

Open strategy workbook →

03

Price integration separately

North Park, The Wisteria and Nine Residences test the value of direct retail and transport integration, not just distance to rail.

Open strategy workbook →

04

Match bedroom and size

Compare bedroom type, floor area and floor band together. PSF alone can make compact launch units look more expensive without showing quantum.

Open strategy workbook →

05

Keep sale states apart

Canberra Crescent is New Sale evidence. Sub Sale and Resale controls include different completion, condition, financing and seller effects.

Open strategy workbook →

06

Treat plans as context

North-South Corridor and Northern Gateway plans support the area thesis, but are not added to achieved prices or presented as guaranteed uplift.

Open strategy workbook →

Research findings

01

Launch evidence is deep

340 official caveats equal 90.4% of 376 project units. This is caveat-to-stock evidence—not developer-confirmed sales or unique buyers.

02

The launch premium is visible

Canberra Crescent's S$1,996 median PSF is 13.2% away from Watergardens' recent non-New-Sale evidence. Sale state and completion explain part of the gap.

03

Closest peers are not identical

Watergardens contributes 75 current-window transactions; The Commodore contributes 37. Bedroom, size and floor tabs are more reliable than their all-unit medians.

04

Integration offers a different trade

North Park's current-window median is S$1,870 PSF. Buyers trade a more established integrated town centre against an older lease clock and Yishun rather than Canberra positioning.

05

Launch path is not appreciation

Monthly Canberra Crescent medians reflect the sequence of released and booked units. Changes across launch months cannot verify capital growth before a resale market exists.

06

District liquidity is mostly resale

Since 2025 the district ledger contains 480 Resale, 103 Sub Sale and 340 New Sale caveats. Exit evidence must be read separately from launch absorption.

Sources and calculation register

Transaction evidence

  • URA Property Market Information: official District 27 caveats.
  • URA REALIS methodology: caveat coverage limitations.
  • Headline window: 2025-01–2026-06; partial 2026-07 retained only in the ledger.
  • Raw official row multiplicity is retained; identical public attributes can represent distinct units.

Project and spatial facts

  • SGX-filed PropNex update: 376 units and 2 August 2025 launch.
  • URA GLS parcel details: 99-year site and planning parameters.
  • OneMap: reviewed project coordinates.
  • LTA rail map: operational MRT network.
  • MOE SchoolFinder: final address-specific school checks.

Calculation register

  • Peer cohort: calendar year × sale state × bedroom count.
  • Project reference: project × calendar year × bedroom count.
  • Size cohort: calendar year × sale state × 100-sqft band.
  • Percentiles use average rank and include the subject row.
  • Bedroom labels are secondary EdgeProp matches; source is shown per row.
Read before deciding. URA caveats are voluntary and not exhaustive. Identical public rows can represent distinct apartment transactions, so official multiplicity is preserved. Exact unit numbers, view, facing, condition, discounts and purchaser identity are unavailable. Bedroom labels are secondary EdgeProp row matches because URA does not publish bedrooms. New Sale, Sub Sale and Resale prices reflect different asset states. Straight-line MRT and school diagnostics are not routed walking distances or official Primary 1 home-school measurements. This is descriptive research, not a valuation or financial recommendation.
